title: Rogue AP — Trunk Port Reconfiguration Confirmed

fields.summary: IT has confirmed that the rogue wireless access point installed in Electrical Room B was not only connected to Port 23 on the Cisco 2960 switch, but also reconfigured that port from an access mode to a trunk mode. This change allows the device to carry traffic from all VLANs — including Server VLAN 10, Admin VLAN 20, Security Camera VLAN 30, Retail VLAN 40, and Management VLAN 99. As a result, any device connecting to the hidden SSID on the rogue AP gains access to the entire internal network. This was not a random or opportunistic act — it required knowledge of switch configuration, default credentials, and NCIA’s VLAN structure. The attacker had deliberate access to network infrastructure. The full reach of the compromise is now confirmed.

actions.text: IT team confirmed the rogue TP-Link device was connected to Port 23 on the Cisco 2960 switch in Electrical Room B.
IT reviewed switch configuration logs and confirmed Port 23 was reconfigured from access to trunk mode.
IT cross-referenced the device's MAC address (50:C7:BF:XX:XX:XX) with known inventory — not in database.
IT confirmed the trunk port now carries traffic from VLANs 10, 20, 30, 40, and 99.
IT issued alert: All network access via Port 23 is now untrusted and must be treated as compromised.

planned: Initiate full network isolation of VLAN 60 (Baggage/OT) and VLAN 99 (Management) pending forensic review.
Audit all switch configurations across Concourse B and Concourse A network closets for unauthorized changes.
Request CISA technical team to assist in forensic analysis of switch configuration logs.
issues: Switch management credentials may be standardized across all closets — if so, attacker could have used them across multiple sites.
No CCTV coverage in Electrical Room B or maintenance corridor — limits forensic visibility.
Rogue device remains active and accessible from Concourse B parking structure.
fields.approvedBy: IT Director, North Coast Regional Airport Authority

instructorNote: This inject confirms the attacker’s technical sophistication. The trunk port reconfiguration is the key to full network compromise. Watch for teams to ask about credential reuse across switch closets.
